A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CARPS framework and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–I. Corresponding methods, experiments, and appendix material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark-subselection results and optimizer evaluations over 20 seeds, including performance heatmaps and statistical rankings in Section 8 and Appendix I.

after.justification: v2 retains original subselection experiments and reports revised optimizer performance results, rankings, and trajectories in Section 8 and Appendix I.

M1.justification: The ask-and-tell interface, task representation, and star-discrepancy subset-selection procedure are retained. Section 7.1 and Appendix G clarify the existing procedure; the revised optimizer roster does not introduce a new proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: The five benchmark collections and four task types remain unchanged. Appendix H's selected-task tables and corresponding task labels in Appendix I match across versions; no new evaluated domain or test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: The blackbox comparison expands from 8 to 13 optimizers, adding SMAC3-HPOFacade and Nevergrad-CMA-ES and replacing the single SyneTune-BO entry with BORE, BOTorch, CQR, and TPE variants. Multi-fidelity comparisons replace SyneTune-SyncMOBSTER and SyneTune-DEHB with SyneTune-BOHB and SyneTune-ASHA. Multi-objective comparisons remove SyneTune-BO-MO-LS, SyneTune-BO-MO-RS, and SyneTune-MOREA. These changes appear in the reported comparisons, including Figures 10–15.

E3.justification: The reported default optimizer settings, dimensionality-based trial budgets, development/test construction, and evaluation procedures are retained. More explicit description of per-task normalization does not establish a change to the existing preprocessing procedure.

E4.justification: Appendix H retains the same subset-size sensitivity plots and development/test ranking-validation tables. The revised benchmark scores and illustrative optimizer example do not introduce a new ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 20 seeds, averaging across seeds, Friedman testing followed by Nemenyi comparisons, and a significance level of 0.05. Updated ranks and critical-difference displays do not establish changed statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Figures 5–7 and 10–17 contain extensively revised costs, rankings, trajectories, and comparator entries. For example, Figure 6 changes Ax's mean cost on BBOB function 11, dimension 16, from 431.727 to 419.778. Figure 17's final-rank legend changes from RandomSearch leading at 2.1 to SMAC3-MOMF-GP leading at 2.1, while remaining nonsignificant. Rank shifts in comparisons with changed optimizer sets are not directly interpretable as performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations 4–5 make normalized coordinates and the origin-anchored box volume explicit. These clarify the normalization and star-discrepancy definition already described in v1; no substantive new assumption, theorem, derivation, or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list revise the advertised optimizer coverage from 28 to 26 variants. The principal contributions—unified benchmarking, representative development/test subsets, and baseline results across four task types—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 8.2 retains the interpretations concerning optimizer complementarity, ranking stability, and caution about insignificant differences; only the illustrative optimizer/task pair changes. Section 9 retains the same applicability limitations and discrepancy-bias discussion.

D1.justification: Section 7.1 explicitly identifies normalization as occurring per task, and Appendix D adds an OptBench example-repository link for benchmark contributions. Hardware, runtime estimates, CARPS version, dependency information, and interface requirements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 3 and Table 2 revise SyneTune's stated capabilities to BB/MF, update its listed benchmarks and optimizer count, and remove the learning-curve criticism. References also change with the optimizer roster, including additions of Bergstra et al. (2011) and Salinas et al. (2023). The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Localized edits clarify hyperparameter terminology, normalization, discrepancy notation, and Appendix G's optimizer examples. An author is added and the acknowledgements are removed. The main narrative and section/appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Critical-difference diagrams gain colored connectors and revised styling; result legends, axes, and heatmap columns accommodate the changed optimizer sets. Figure 3 receives revised labeling and an expanded explanatory caption, and several figures move. The existing display types and overall layout are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves explanatory clarity and result consistency. Section 7.1 and Figure 3 explain previously terse notation and labels. In Figure 17, the final-rank legend now agrees with the critical-difference diagram and displayed heatmap values, resolving a visible inconsistency in v1. The gain is limited by reduced multi-objective comparator coverage and unresolved subset-size inconsistencies between Section 7.2 and Appendix H.
